findings.desc: CHK-015:edge:1 (matcher count bound is policy-resolved, not hardcoded): no fixture in red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs or the smoke validates the matcher-count bound under a policy with a DIFFERENT policy.maxMatchers value. Every other floor claim of this kind in the same story (rule-2 length/entropy floors in red-w2d-specificity-conjunction.mjs via a raised-minMatcherLen policy, the class registry in CHK-016 via a CUSTOM matcherClassRegistry, policyDigest content-sensitivity in CHK-010 via an otherPolicy) IS proven with a two-policy differential; only the CHK-015 count bound is proven solely against the frozen default (maxMatchers=8), so a hard-coded 8 in place of policy.maxMatchers would pass every committed test. The binder self-flagged this exact gap in its own evidence note.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: two-policy differential added - an identical 4-matcher envelope is accepted at maxMatchers=8 and rejected at 3, with the message asserted to carry policy.maxMatchers=3, so a hard-coded 8 can no longer pass.

findings.desc: CHK-012 read-only claim (packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-command-readonly.mjs, packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts section 7): the handler doc comment on red_evidence_envelope_check (packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts ~line 349) asserts the command spawns no RED run and its only child processes are the W2b binding readers git rev-parse/git show. No committed test verifies this: the mechanism used (a per-file SHA-256 snapshot of .lattice/ taken before and after the call) can only detect writes under .lattice/; it does not intercept, mock, or otherwise observe child_process.spawn/exec/spawnSync calls, so a regression that caused the handler to shell out to run a test (e.g. code drifted toward the reserved-for-later runner leaf) would pass this regression undetected even though it violates the storys core before a run is ever spent safety property. Given this is the single most safety-critical claim of the whole command, the read-only regression should intercept/spy on child_process to positively prove no RED-run-shaped spawn occurs, not rely solely on directory-hash absence-of-evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed together with F-012 and F-013 (same defect, three hosts converged). The snapshot claim is narrowed to exactly what it proves, AND a child_process recorder now asserts the real spawn set. The recorder falsified the old docstring enumeration: repository/worktree resolution also runs git rev-parse --show-toplevel, --git-common-dir and git worktree list --porcelain beyond the W2b rev-parse/show. All read-only; the git read is untouched and the docstring's narrow claim (spawns no RED run) was not weakened.

findings.desc: CHK-013:happy:0 literal intent text reads: red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts listed in lattice.config.json validate.commands and lattice validate runs it successfully. The bound evidence (packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-validate-registration.mjs) only statically enumerates dist/tasks/red-evidence-* on disk and cross-checks it against the validate.commands array in config; it never invokes the lattice validate command itself. CHK-013:happy:1 separately runs the smoke by direct node invocation (node packages/main/dist/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.js), not through the lattice validate pipeline. So no committed evidence in this story exercises the actual validate-pipeline invocation path (spawn args/cwd/timeout handling for this entry) end to end; the binder self-flagged this exact gap (lattice validate was not run for this binding). Registration-in-config + direct-invocation-passes only jointly approximate the literal intent, and this exact substitution pattern was previously used for the same reason in W2c (red-w2c-validate-registration.mjs), so it is a known, repeated, but still real gap against the literal command the intent names.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: red-w2d-command-readonly section 8 now resolves the entry via configuredValidationCommands and executes it through runValidationCommand - the two functions lattice validate itself uses - asserting exit 0, instead of only checking config registration statically.

findings.desc: CHK-002 closed-enum rejections (stream, polarity, greenExempt legality) and CHK-001 identity/kind rejections are exercised only against kind:literal-line matchers across red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs and the smoke; no fixture asserts an invalid stream, invalid polarity, or illegal greenExempt on a kind:class matcher. In envelope.ts these checks (validateAssertionEnvelope lines ~317-337) run unconditionally before the kind-specific branch, so the current implementation is not actually kind-differentiated, but the committed matrix does not prove that: a future change that moved these checks inside the literal-line-only branch (mirroring how value-byte-length checks are correctly literal-line-only) would silently stop rejecting a malformed class matcher stream/polarity/greenExempt, and no committed test would catch it.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: the full closed-enum table (5 streams, 4 polarities, greenExempt x3, duplicate id across kinds) is re-run against kind:'class' matchers, each rejection asserted by code.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts:346-348 (matcher-value-empty) tags an EMPTY literal-line value as R1-3. Spec places non-emptiness under §1.3 rule 1 ("value MUST be stored trimmed (§1.1.1), MUST be non-empty, and MUST NOT be a member of policy.forbiddenCatchAlls", spec:401-403), which is the §1.3 minimum-specificity rule that R1-2 owns ("a degenerate/blocklisted literal", spec:495-498). R1-3s own enumerated list (spec:499-504) explicitly names only value longer than maxMatcherLen or carrying leading/trailing whitespace for value-bound failures — it never mentions empty/too-short. The codebase itself already applies this exact reasoning to the two sibling clauses of the same rule-1 triple: trimmed -> R1-3 (explicitly named in R1-3s list) and blocklisted -> R1-2 (explicitly named in R1-2s list, per envelope.ts:393-400). non-empty is the third clause and is NOT named in R1-3s list, so by the codes own established methodology it should route to R1-2 like blocklisted, not R1-3 like trimmed. Failing input: matchers:[{id:L1,kind:literal-line,value:"",stream:combined,polarity:present-in-red}] -> current output tags matcher-value-empty as R1-3; expected R1-2 per §1.3 rule 1. This choice is pinned into 3 committed regressions (red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs:219-221, red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts:298), so it is a systematic mistag, not a slip.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed together with F-006 (same defect, behavior lane and codex host-B converged). An empty literal moved out of the bounds layer into the section 1.3 block and is now tagged R1-2. The argument that settled it: the code already split the other two clauses of the same rule-1 triple correctly - trimmed to R1-3 because R1-3's enumeration names it, blocklisted to R1-2 because R1-2's does - and 'non-empty' is absent from R1-3's enumeration, so it routes to R1-2 by the module's own existing logic.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #2, orchestrator-verified] An empty literal value is tagged R1-3 but the spec assigns it R1-2. Section 1.6's R1-3 trigger enumeration covers a value LONGER than maxMatcherLen or carrying leading/trailing whitespace - it does not cover an empty value. Section 1.3 rule 1 explicitly requires value to be non-empty, and rule-1 failures are R1-2. red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs currently pins the wrong tag, which freezes the error. Fix the tag and the fixture.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed - see B-9ff1:F-005, the same defect reported independently by codex host-B. Empty literal now tagged R1-2; the matrix fixture that pinned the wrong tag was corrected too, since a fixture pinning a wrong tag freezes the error.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #4, orchestrator-verified against spec text] greenExempt:false on a non-present-in-red matcher is accepted; it must reject. Section 1.1 states greenExempt is 'legal ONLY on polarity present-in-red matchers (any other polarity CARRYING IT is rejected)' - the test is whether the field is PRESENT, not whether it is true. The implementer's documented ambiguity resolution 5 reasoned that false cannot change assertion identity under section 0.4 and therefore accepted it; that reasoning is wrong on this clause. Reject on presence regardless of value, and add the fixture.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: the guard is now presence-based (else if polarity !== 'present-in-red'), matching section 1.1's 'any other polarity CARRYING IT is rejected' - the test is whether the field is present, not whether it is true. The implementer's earlier ambiguity note reasoning from section 0.4 identity was wrong on this clause and the header note was rewritten.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #5, orchestrator-verified] testCaseRef is never matched against the adapter's registered testCaseRefPattern. Section 1.2 (argv resolution) states: match testCaseRef against testCaseRefPattern; no match rejects R1-5. This is envelope-decidable - the pattern lives in the resolved policy registry and the testCaseRef is in the envelope - so it belongs in the same R1-5 check that already validates adapter registration. Failing input: adapterId npm-script@1 with testCaseRef 'free-form:not-derived' currently returns ok:true.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: testCaseRef is now matched against the resolved adapter's testCaseRefPattern, no match rejecting R1-5 per section 1.2 argv resolution. Six pattern-mismatch fixtures plus a cross-adapter row where the same ref is rejected under node-test@1 and accepted under npm-script@1.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts:274-434: the matcherSetEvaluable gate (line 385, requiring rawMatchers.length in [1,maxMatchers] AND bounded.length>0) suppresses the ENTIRE §1.3 block — per-matcher rule1/2 AND the rule-3 class-only-present-in-red check — whenever the matcher COUNT is out of bounds. This contradicts the modules own documented invariant at envelope.ts:236-237 ("Every check runs — nothing short-circuits — so co-occurring faults are ALL reported and no tag suppresses another"). Concrete failing input verified against dist: an envelope with 9 matchers (policy.maxMatchers=8) where the sole present-in-red matcher is a class matcher (stderr-nonempty) and the other 8 are valid present-in-green literals — this genuinely violates §1.3 rule 3 (a class matcher can never be the sole present-in-red evidence, spec:411-414, tag R1-2) in addition to the count-bound R1-3. validateAssertionEnvelope returns ONLY [{tag:R1-3,code:matcher-count-above-maximum}] — the R1-2 rule-3 violation is silently dropped, never surfaced to the operator. Verified by direct probe against packages/main/dist/core/red-evidence/envelope.js (matches src at HEAD). R1-1 is unaffected (computed independently, still fires alongside R1-3 when co-occurring — confirmed by a second probe), so this is specific to the R1-2 §1.3 block. None of the 3 committed regressions (red-w2d-rejection-matrix.mjs, red-w2d-specificity-conjunction.mjs, red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts) construct an over/under-count fixture that ALSO carries a rule1/2/3 violation, so the gap is untested as well as unimplemented.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed - the finding no other reviewer or the orchestrator caught. matcherSetEvaluable was rawMatchers.length in [1,maxMatchers] AND bounded.length>0, so a count violation suppressed the ENTIRE section 1.3 block including rule 3. It is now bounded.length>0 only; the count bound is reported independently and unconditionally. Orchestrator verified empirically against dist: 9 matchers with the sole present-in-red being a class matcher now reports R1-3/matcher-count-above-maximum AND R1-2/present-in-red-not-admissible-literal together, where before only R1-3 appeared. Two guards added against over-correcting.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #6, orchestrator-verified] Absolute-path detection recognizes only a leading slash. Section 1.1.3 requires targetArtifactRef to be slash-normalized AND RELATIVE, rejecting an absolute path at envelope schema time as R1-3. Failing input: targetArtifactRef 'C:/outside' is slash-normalized and absolute yet returns ok:true. Reject non-relative forms generally, not just the POSIX leading-slash form.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: DRIVE_QUALIFIED_PREFIX rejects C:/, C:\\ and C:x, so absolute detection is no longer only the POSIX leading-slash form, per section 1.1.3's slash-normalized AND relative requirement. Seven new bad-path rows including C:/outside, plus an accept row for weird:name/dist/x.js so the rule is not degraded into 'reject any colon'.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #7, orchestrator-verified] supplementaryArtifact:null is treated as absent. Section 0.4 states every optional field is OMITTED entirely when absent and is NEVER written as null or empty string, so an explicit null is a malformed envelope rather than an omission. Failing input: supplementaryArtifact:null returns ok:true; it must reject.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: an explicit supplementaryArtifact null is rejected as supplementary-artifact-null (R1-3), per section 0.4's rule that optional fields are omitted entirely and never written as null. Paired with an omitted-entirely accept contrast row.

findings.desc: [codex host-B #8 CONVERGED with test-coverage F-002] The read-only regression cannot prove what it claims. Its mechanism is a before/after SHA-256 snapshot of .lattice/, which detects writes there and nothing else; it never intercepts child_process, so it cannot detect a spawned process. ORCHESTRATOR ADJUDICATION: the handler DOES spawn git via the W2b committed-binding reader (target-bindings.ts runGit uses spawnSync), and that is CORRECT and deliberate - reading the binding from the committed tree rather than the live directory is W2b's anti-swap property. The DEV handoff's phrase 'no process spawning' was too absolute and is not a code defect. What must be fixed is the EVIDENCE: either narrow the claim to what the snapshot proves (no writes under .lattice, no chain record, no gate change) or genuinely assert the spawn set. Do not remove the git read.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed - see B-9ff1:F-002. Orchestrator adjudication recorded there: the git spawn is CORRECT and deliberate (W2b reads the binding from the committed tree rather than the live directory, an anti-swap property), so the DEV handoff phrase 'no process spawning' was an orchestrator wording error rather than a code defect. What was fixed is the evidence, not the behaviour.

findings.desc: packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-command-readonly.mjs:126-141 and packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts:386-398: the committed read-only proof snapshots per-file SHA-256 hashes of the .lattice tree before/after invoking red_evidence_envelope_check, plus static registry-flag assertions (ownershipClass readOnly, READ_ONLY_COMMANDS membership). Neither technique can detect an errant child-process spawn that writes nothing under .lattice (e.g. outside the repo, to a temp dir, or a network call) — a directory hash and a static classification flag are not behavioral evidence against process spawning. This is a test-assurance gap, not a functional defect: direct source reading confirms the only child processes in the call path are the two read-only git commands (rev-parse/show) inside readCommittedTargetBindings (packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/target-bindings.ts:141,172,180), and the handlers own docstring (packages/main/src/handlers/red-evidence.ts:347-355) correctly and narrowly claims spawns no RED run rather than an absolute spawns nothing claim. Flagging per the review brief item 4 (a test that only hashes a directory cannot detect a process spawn) so the gap between what is claimed and what the regression can actually detect is on record; no code change is indicated, only stronger test assurance (e.g. intercepting child_process.spawn/spawnSync during the check() calls and asserting only git rev-parse/show occur) would close it.
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of B-9ff1:F-002 and B-9ff1:F-012 - the same read-only test-assurance gap, reported independently by three hosts (test-coverage, codex host-B, behavior). Resolved by the fix recorded under F-002.

findings.desc: Empirical read-only check (post-merge, unaffected by the merge — cli-engine.ts and stale-detector.ts have 0 commits in d47a35787d..HEAD): running node bin/lattice.js red_evidence_envelope_check against B-9ff1 (which is genuinely stale in REVIEW) DID append a row to .lattice/activity.jsonl, contradicting the literal comment at packages/main/src/cli/activity-policy.ts:23-25 ('It must append NOTHING (no hook, no activity log, no process event)'). Root cause: cli-engine.ts writeLog is gated by 'shouldWriteActivityLog(cmd, parsed) || staleWarnings.length > 0' (line 1416/1488) — the staleWarnings OR-clause bypasses the READ_ONLY_COMMANDS suppression for EVERY read-only command (not specific to red_evidence_envelope_check), by design, for stale-state trend analysis, and is self-limited by a cooldown (suppressRecentlyEmittedWarnings in stale-detector.ts) so it fires at most once per cooldown window. Verified: a second story_get call immediately after (same stale story) did NOT re-append, confirming the cooldown, not red_evidence_envelope_check-specific misbehavior. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this predates B-9ff1 entirely (packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts and core/stale-detector.ts are untouched in the whole d47a35787d..HEAD range, so it already existed when RP-003 passed pre-merge) and is shared uniformly by all ~90 READ_ONLY_COMMANDS members, not introduced or worsened by this story or by the merge. The formal guarantee the story actually makes in command-policy.ts (line 445: executes no envelope, writes no artifact/process event/chain record, and changes no gate verdict) remains TRUE and verified — activity.jsonl is generic CLI session telemetry, not one of those four enumerated categories, and no gate/verdict/artifact/chain state is touched. Recommend softening the activity-policy.ts comment's absolute no-activity-log wording rather than any functional change. Repro: cd worktree; run node bin/lattice.js red_evidence_envelope_check --storyId=B-9ff1 --assertionFile=<any path> --json while the story is stale, and diff a full .lattice/ shasum snapshot before/after — activity.jsonl hash changes.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit b63dcad96b86de010dfc3be10e48e14016cb2428 (comment-only, one file, 11 insertions / 3 deletions in packages/main/src/cli/activity-policy.ts). The finding is REAL and was independently reproduced by the main agent rather than accepted on the reviewer's word: grep -c red_evidence_envelope_check .lattice/activity.jsonl returns 20, so the command has in fact appended activity rows. Root cause: the writeLog call sites in cli-engine.ts read shouldWriteActivityLog(cmd, parsed) || staleWarnings.length > 0, and the right-hand disjunct is an independent path that bypasses READ_ONLY_COMMANDS suppression for ANY command, read-only included, whenever the story carries an uncooled stale warning (STALE_WARNING_COOLDOWN_MS = 30 minutes, core/stale-detector.ts). shouldWriteActivityLog itself is correct and does return false for members. What was defective was this story's OWN comment, added by GREEN commit e88bb78a65, which asserted the command must append NOTHING including no activity log and that membership guarantees exactly that. Membership is necessary but not sufficient, so the assertion was false as written, and it was the only absolute claim of its kind in that file. The comment now states what membership actually guarantees, names the stale-warning bypass and its cooldown by file and symbol rather than by line number, and records that the formal contract in core/command-policy.ts (writes no artifact, no process event, no chain record, changes no gate verdict) holds unconditionally because activity.jsonl is generic CLI session telemetry outside those four categories. Marked partially_mitigated rather than fixed because the underlying cli-engine bypass is deliberately NOT repaired here: making the stale-warning path respect READ_ONLY_COMMANDS would change shared behaviour for roughly ninety commands and is out of this story's scope; that systemic defect is filed as separate follow-up work. Verification after the change: build clean, npx tsc --noEmit clean, red-evidence-envelope-smoke OK, and all five packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-*.mjs pass.

findings.desc: activity-policy.ts:23-33 (the F-014 repair, commit b63dcad96b) states as an unconditional fact that 'Membership here makes shouldWriteActivityLog (this file) return false' for red_evidence_envelope_check. That is only true when process.env.LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY !== '1' — shouldWriteActivityLog (same file, lines 151-159) returns, for any read-only command, exactly `process.env.LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY === '1'`, i.e. false by default but TRUE when that var is set. LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY=1 is not an obscure test knob: it is this repo's own documented 'global-fallback' Codex entrypoint env (init-assets.ts:148-163 LATTICE_CODEX_ADAPTER_MANIFEST.recommendedEntrypoints, init-assets.ts:213-238 CODEX_README template, core/codex-adapter-checks.ts:57/502/607 GLOBAL_CODEX_FALLBACK_COMMAND), recommended precisely when a Codex session lacks the local wrapper. Under that real, documented, in-repo operating mode, red_evidence_envelope_check membership in READ_ONLY_COMMANDS does NOT make shouldWriteActivityLog return false — it makes it return true, and every invocation appends an activity.jsonl row. This is the same class of overclaim (a classification-driven guarantee stated as unconditional when a real code path flips it) that this very comment was rewritten this round to stop making about the staleWarnings bypass — the new text names that bypass explicitly but omits this second, equally real one on the very sentence introducing the primary claim.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit ee73b9f66df8ac0ba91b81ef2ab8a455287f3735. The F-014 repair comment in packages/main/src/cli/activity-policy.ts named only the stale-warning bypass and still asserted unconditionally that membership makes shouldWriteActivityLog return false. It now states that membership settles two surfaces outright (hooks and process events, both gated on isReadOnlyCommand alone) and explicitly does NOT settle the activity log, then names BOTH bypasses. This finding and F-020 are the same defect found independently by two lanes. The underlying fact, verified independently by the main agent and not taken on the reviewer's word: membership in READ_ONLY_COMMANDS is necessary but NOT sufficient to suppress an activity-log row. Two independent bypasses exist. (1) shouldWriteActivityLog returns process.env.LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY === '1' for read-only commands, and that variable is not a test knob: it is baked into GLOBAL_CODEX_FALLBACK_COMMAND in core/codex-adapter-checks.ts and into the generated Codex wrapper in src/init-assets.ts. (2) Both writeLog call sites in cli-engine.ts read shouldWriteActivityLog(cmd, parsed) || staleWarnings.length > 0, and the right disjunct appends one generic session row for ANY command while the story carries an uncooled stale warning (STALE_WARNING_COOLDOWN_MS, 30 minutes, core/stale-detector.ts). Empirically .lattice/activity.jsonl held 20 rows for this command when the defect was found and 28 by the time it was repaired. What remains unconditionally true is the core/command-policy.ts contract: no artifact, no process event, no chain record, and no gate verdict change. The hook and process-event suppressions are also genuinely unconditional, because both are gated on isReadOnlyCommand alone with no second term - those clauses were kept, not weakened. Deliberately NOT repaired here: the shared cli-engine bypass itself. Making the stale-warning path respect READ_ONLY_COMMANDS would change behaviour for roughly ninety commands and is filed as separate follow-up work. Also left alone as sibling-story material: the six 'Nothing written.' refusal strings belonging to the W2b/W2c mutating chain commands, and the F-028 usage_sweep comment from story B-70e9 - both filed separately. Verification after the change: build clean, npx tsc --noEmit clean, red-evidence-envelope-smoke OK, and all five packages/main/tests/red/red-w2d-*.mjs pass. A second commit 63a9092d7fbfe41b15a3f825f231333e91a3782f widened the repair beyond the reviewers' file list after the implementer reported three more instances of the same absolute for this same command, one of them user-facing: the catalog description in cli/command-catalog.ts surfaced through help, the phase-bucket comment in core/config.ts, and the registration comment in registry.ts. Leaving a user-visible 'writes nothing' in the catalog while fixing the printed strings would have been inconsistent.

findings.desc: red-w2d-command-readonly.mjs section 6a (lines 274-281) snapshots the whole .lattice/ tree before/after 8 calls to check()=registeredCheck(args)=registry.get('red_evidence_envelope_check')(args), and its own docstring (CHK-012 item 1, lines 19-29) asserts this 'covers the story record, the chain, evidence artifacts and process-event logs, because those all live there.' registry.get(cmd) returns the raw handler and is invoked directly here — it never goes through cli-engine.ts's outer run() wrapper, which is the exact code containing the two writeLog call sites (cli-engine.ts lines 1416 and 1488) that OR in staleWarnings.length > 0. [codex host-B C2] Verified by main agent. Blanket 'runs no hook' is false: only preCommand (cli-engine.ts runHooks preCommand) and postCommand are gated on !isReadOnlyCommand. The onError call site has no such predicate - its only guard is config0?.hooks?.onError - so a configured onError hook DOES run whenever the command throws. The inadmissible-envelope path throws by design, so this is the command's PRIMARY failure route, not an edge case. Four Claude lanes each verified the two gated call sites and generalised from them; none found the third. Affected: handlers/red-evidence.ts docstring, tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts registration assertion, tests/red/red-w2d-command-readonly.mjs header and assertion.

[codex host-B C3] Verified by main agent. The handler's top docstring says an inadmissible verdict is surfaced by throwing 'rather than recording the verdict anywhere'. False: the handler throws the complete rendered rejection report, the CLI catch path passes e.message into writeLog, and writeLog stores it in the activity row's error field.
